# CHAKRAVYUH demo report (generated by scripts/run_demo.py -- do not edit)

Scenario: **amphan_2020** - Cyclone Amphan, 16-20 May 2020 — Odisha / West Bengal / Bangladesh coast
Horizon 7500 min, 15-minute ticks, 15 scripted events (7 from the source release, 8 constructed by us).

## Limits (read first)

- **The timeline is real; the network is not.** Every `t_minutes` is computed from the
  timestamps in the IMD RSMC press release on Amphan, and the warned districts are the
  ones that release names. What is constructed is the per-cell state: no public dataset
  records cell-site outage for any Indian cyclone, so cell counts are scaled from
  reported aggregates (COAI: ~8,500 towers / ~36,000 BTS, 65-70% capacity on day 3) and
  the per-cell outages are ours. So are the rumour and the forged order, which are
  adversarial tests and not historical events. Every constructed event carries
  `synthetic: true` and is greyed in the UI.
- Property thresholds are **illustrative**, not legal or engineering standards.
- Policy packs are **encodings of selected clauses for simulation. They are not legal
  advice** and they are not a complete statement of any jurisdiction's law.
- Clause records whose `verbatim_status` is `unverified_summary` carry an accurate summary
  with a real source URL, **not the verbatim text of the instrument**. See `docs/kb_report.md`.
- Units are illustrative (cells, minutes, percentages). No money, no casualties, no
  confidence intervals.

| `bangladesh` | PASS (+40) | PASS (+0) | PASS (+345) | FAIL (-855) | yes |

| `india_current` | FAIL (-60) | FAIL (-1) | FAIL (-7140) | FAIL (-855) | yes |

Margin is signed slack in each property's own illustrative unit; negative means
violated. Units per property:

- **P1**: During any suspension, relief/emergency traffic in affected cells stays reachable _(unit: % of affected cells reachable for relief)_
- **P2**: No irreversible action executes on an unauthenticated (forged) order _(unit: irreversible executions on an unauthenticated order (fewer is better))_
- **P3**: Every affected area, including across the border, gets a public alert within T_alert of the warning, in a local language _(unit: minutes from first warning to a valid local-language alert)_
- **P4**: Disaster roaming is active in affected circles within T_roam of landfall _(unit: minutes from landfall to roaming active)_

## Gap register (domain-first, country as instance)

| Gap (domain-first) | Class | Property | Instance | Responsible clauses | Passes under |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Emergency telecom: A suspension direction carries no mandatory carve-out for relief and emergency traffic, and priority routing is permitted rather than obliged, so a lawful suspension can switch off the very traffic the response depends on. | policy | P1 | India (WB-KOLKATA) | IN.TA2023.s20.1, INTL.ITU.CONST.art40, INTL.ITU.E106 | bangladesh, fcc_mdri |
| Emergency telecom: No instrument requires an operator to authenticate a service-suspension direction before giving effect to it, so a forged direction executes exactly like a genuine one and the irreversible act is complete before any verification occurs. | policy | P2 | India (WB-KOLKATA) | IN.SUSP2024.r3, IN.TA2023.s20.2, IN.TCSR2024.no_order_auth | bangladesh, fcc_mdri |
| Emergency telecom: No standing cross-border trigger: no instrument empowers any actor to issue a public alert across the border in time, and the domestic alerting/roaming power is scoped to domestic areas only. | policy | P3 | India-Bangladesh (BD-KHULNA) | IN.DMA2005.s6, IN.NDMA.CAP.SACHET | bangladesh, fcc_mdri |
| Emergency telecom: No standing cross-border trigger: no instrument empowers any actor to enable disaster roaming across the border in time, and the domestic alerting/roaming power is scoped to domestic areas only. | policy | P4 | India-Bangladesh (BD-KHULNA) | IN.DOTSOP2020.icr, IN.UL.DISASTER | fcc_mdri |
